editorial:
You follow Kentaro and Keiko as they dig into the life of their grandfather, a World War II kamikaze pilot. What starts as family research turns into a mystery, because the men who knew him tell very different stories. Some remember him as careful and afraid, while others see a brave pilot. The movie moves between present-day interviews and wartime flashbacks, so you slowly piece together who he really was. It has a serious, emotional tone, but it also keeps you curious about the next clue. If you like family secrets and war stories, this one pulls you in without feeling like a dry history lesson.

The acting feels grounded, and the flight scenes are tense without going over the top. The pacing is steady, though the back-and-forth timeline can feel a little long in spots. The emotional payoff is strong if you stick with it. Watch it if you enjoy character-driven war dramas and do not mind subtitles. For the best picture, stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Kentaro and Keiko learn their grandfather was not a coward. He had delayed his kamikaze mission to protect younger pilots and keep his promise to return home. When the time came, he chose to fly the final mission himself. The twist is that his careful, life-loving nature was the real courage, not reckless bravery. He dies as a hero who sacrificed himself to save others, and the siblings finally understand his true character.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character-driven war dramas and family mysteries.
